title: Introduce 'parachute' fairness path + time-slicer for continuous batcher to reduce starvation and tail spikes
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation:
Under mixed-tenant continuous-batching workloads we observed recurring p99 amplification driven by long-waiting small KV-heavy requests that progressively starve latency-sensitive short requests. Existing fairshare logic prevents absolute starvation but is slow to recover under sudden shifts and can introduce microbursts that push kernel hotspots.

This PR introduces a lightweight 'parachute' fairness path and a complementary time-slicer for the continuous batcher scheduler. Goals: reduce p99 tail under mixed KV/text workloads, minimize added scheduling overhead, and provide an emergency rescue path that temporarily overrides soft reservations without violating throughput targets.

What changed (high level):
- Add ParachuteCoordinator: monitors per-queue wait ages and issues short-duration soft reservations (parachute slots) to starving queues when a configurable age threshold is crossed. Parachute reservations are ephemeral and decay with linear backoff.
- Add TimeSlicer core to the batcher worker loop: enforces sub-slot time quanta (configurable) to prevent long single-request monopolies; cooperative yield points added near KV prefetch and compile/kernel selection.
- Priority aging adjustment: integrator that increases effective priority for requests as they age, bounded by a safety cap to limit oscillation.
- Timeout jitter + rampback: when parachute slots trigger, we apply jittered soft-timeouts to the owning request to encourage early fallback to smaller model variant or preemptible mode.
- KV prefetch hinting: when a parachute slot is granted, the KV prefetcher is signalled to preferentially warm keys for the rescued queue to reduce post-rescue cold misses.
- Metrics, dashboards, and perf tests: new metrics (parachute_grants, parachute_duration_seconds, timeslice_yields) and Grafana panels + alert rule tweaks.

Design notes and constraints:
- Parachute path is explicitly conservative: grants are small (default 3 tokens equivalent) and only allowed when cluster-wide slowdowns are detected or when queue age crosses the threshold. This minimizes risk of throughput regressions.
- TimeSlicer is cooperative; hot paths that cannot yield (legacy kernels) are detected at startup and excluded from timeslicing to avoid correctness regressions.
- Interactions with the existing admission controller: parachute grants are implemented as additive soft reservations that cannot push the global reserved slots beyond a safety fraction (configurable per cluster).

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for ParachuteCoordinator state transitions and for time-slice boundary conditions.
- Integration test harness: synthetic mixed workload (80% short chat-turns, 20% long KV-heavy rerank jobs) ran for 12h in benchmark-lab; validated stability and absence of oscillation.
- Perf results (benchmark-lab, p99 latency; median across 5 runs):
  - Baseline (main): p99 = 480ms, median = 34ms, throughput = 1000 qps
  - This PR (defaults): p99 = 355ms (-26%), median = 36ms (+6%), throughput = 1060 qps (+6%)
  - Stress case (sudden 4x KV-heavy spike): p99 = 620ms baseline vs 415ms this PR (-33%)

    worker.yield_to_scheduler();
  }

Review thread (summary):
- Ethan: requested stronger tests around backoff behavior and suggested a hard cap on concurrent parachute grants per host.
- Liang: asked for safety proof that parachute grants cannot push cluster reserved capacity beyond safety_fraction. Added explicit guard and unit tests.
- Priya: flagged risk for on-prem upgrade—requested feature-flag and migration doc. Added runtime flag and runbook.
- CI flake: a flaky e2e failing on the first run (timeout in bench harness); rerun passed.

Notes on tuning knobs (defaults):
- parachute.age_threshold_ms = 1200
- parachute.max_concurrent_per_host = 8
- parachute.grant_tokens = 3
- timeslice.quanta_ms = 8
- timeslice.exempt_kernels = ["legacy_cuda_attention_v1"]

Release notes (short):
"Add a parachute fairness path and cooperative timeslicing to the continuous batcher. Improves p99 under mixed KV/text workloads; gated behind a runtime feature flag. See runbook for tuning"
